sections.h2: Why does selling in Pompano Beach differ from selling elsewhere in Broward?
sections.html:
Pompano Beach is a beach city in the north of Broward County, and the city's own resident page says it spans over 25 square miles, halfway between Miami and Palm Beach. The same page counts over 101,400 residents for most of the year and over 150,000 once part-time owners return for winter.

That seasonal pulse shapes a sale. Showings pick up while snowbirds are in town, and an empty house can sit quietly through summer. Owners with deferred repairs, a tenant or an unpaid lien usually weigh three paths.

  • An agent listing, with repair requests, open houses and a closing date tied to the buyer's lender.
  • A direct sale to a neighbor or relative, where you carry the pricing and paperwork.
  • A cash offer for the house in its current shape, with the closing day chosen by the seller.

sections.h2: What local history and land use sit behind Pompano Beach neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Pompano was already a town when Broward County formed on October 1, 1915, and Broward had only three incorporated places that day: Dania, Pompano and Fort Lauderdale. The Florida East Coast Railway reached Palm Beach in 1894 and Miami in 1896, and farming settlements grew up along those tracks, Pompano among them.

Before that, Pompano belonged to Palm Beach County, which became Florida's 47th county on July 1, 1909 with Pompano as its southernmost town. Broward then split away partly over a dispute on alcohol sales and partly because northern Dade residents felt their tax dollars favored Miami, and the county takes its name from a governor who championed Everglades drainage, according to the city's historical pages.

A large piece of the city's layout comes from the Pompano Beach Air Park, which began as a World War II satellite training field for the naval air station at today's Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood airport. The city took it over on August 29, 1947, and the city's airport page says the Air Park now totals 650 acres after land went to schools, a mall site in 1968, a sports complex and a 2007 transfer that includes part of the golf course, Community Park and a fire station.

For a seller, that history shows up in a few concrete ways.

  • Homes near the Air Park may hear aircraft, and the city publishes quiet-flying guidelines because of the effect on residential areas.
  • Properties near Copans Road and the NE 5th Avenue railway line sit in a mixed corridor of homes, parks and public facilities.
  • Buyers often ask about school zoning for Pompano Beach Elementary and Pompano Beach High, both built on former Air Park land.

sections.h2: How did Pompano Beach get its name and its housing mix?
sections.html:
The city's historical pages say a survey crew working for the canal and railway companies around 1880 wrote the word pompano on a map, and the settlement kept it. The town incorporated in 1908, and Beach joined the name on June 16, 1947, after the oceanfront settlement was annexed.

Growth came in layers. The Census Bureau counted 99,845 people in 2010 and 112,046 in 2020, then estimated 117,211 for July 2025. Older single-family blocks, mid-century duplexes and newer condo and townhome projects now share the same city, so a flat citywide price tells you little about one address.

The city markets its 1,000-foot fishing pier, redeveloped beachside fishing village and the early-1900s Hillsboro Lighthouse near the inlet. Properties close to the water raise flood-zone and insurance questions, so gather your policy, any elevation certificate and permits for roof, window or seawall work before a buyer asks.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about homes in Pompano Beach?
sections.html:
They describe a city split almost evenly between owners and renters, with about 4,664 people per square mile in 2020. Commutes average 27.1 minutes, and 83.7 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

sections.h2: What does the Broward homestead exemption mean when I sell in Pompano Beach?
sections.html:
It ends with your ownership. Broward's property appraiser states that the seller's exemptions do not continue beyond the year of the sale, so the next occupant files fresh.

Broward lists a March 1 filing deadline each year, and September 20, 2027 as the hard late-filing cutoff for the 2027 year. The office warns that renting a house out would likely cost the exemption and that unreported changes can bring back taxes, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.

Florida re-values a property after a change of ownership, so a buyer's first bill often runs above yours. The Department of Revenue says a sale, foreclosure or title transfer starts that reset, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses.

  • Keep the annual receipt Broward mails each January.
  • Cancel the exemption on a house you no longer occupy.
  • Ask about portability if you are moving to another Florida homestead within three tax years.

sections.h2: Do the November 2026 amendment results affect a Pompano Beach sale?
sections.html:
They can shape what buyers will pay. A Volusia property appraiser explainer reports that voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, lifting the non-school homestead exemption to as much as $150,000 for 2027 and $250,000 for 2028, and cutting the non-homestead cap to 5 percent.

It adds that implementing legislation will settle some details, so ask Broward's property appraiser how the changes will reach your parcel.

sections.h2: What costs and paperwork come with a deed in Pompano Beach?
sections.html:
Florida taxes a deed at 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county but Miami-Dade. Every party to the document is liable, so the purchase contract settles who pays.

The Broward clerk records the deed and collects that tax. Section 28.24 sets a first-page recording charge of $5.00 and $4.00 per added page, before technology surcharges, so request a quote.

  • Obtain payoff statements from each mortgage and lien holder.
  • Ask the closing agent to prorate the Broward tax bill.
  • Check city permit and code records for open items.
  • Arrange two witnesses for the signing, which Florida requires for land conveyances.

sections.h2: What if the Pompano Beach house has tenants, a foreclosure case or an heir?
sections.html:
Each situation can sell, on its own clock. A month-to-month tenancy ends with 30 days' notice (section 83.57), and unpaid rent starts with a three-day written notice (section 83.56).

In foreclosure, the clerk's sale follows final judgment by 20 to 35 days unless extended (section 45.031). Closing first protects your equity.

For an heir, summary administration fits an estate of $150,000 or less, or a death over two years ago (section 735.201).

faqs.q: Is a cash offer quicker than an agent listing here?
faqs.a: Often yes, since no lender appraisal is involved. Title must still be clear, with liens paid and the deed witnessed and recorded in Broward.

faqs.q: Who covers the deed stamps on a Pompano Beach sale?
faqs.a: The sale contract decides, though the state holds every party liable. The rate is 70 cents per $100 outside Miami-Dade.

faqs.q: Will my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Broward's property appraiser says it stops with the sale year, and the buyer applies anew before March 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell while I am behind on the mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes, if the closing beats the clerk's foreclosure sale. Move early, since that sale can come 20 to 35 days after judgment.
At the Broward County clerk's office, which also collects stamp tax at recording. Bring the signed deed and the fee.
